holidays.name: National Presidential Joke Day
holidays.description: A day for swapping jokes about presidents, politicians and the circus of public life. Bring your best one-liners and your thickest skin, because nobody in office is safe.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite for comedians, speechwriters and anyone who enjoys political humor.
holidays.funFact: Abraham Lincoln was famous for his storytelling and wit, and he often used humor to make a point or ease tension in tough moments.

holidays.name: Play In The Sand Day
holidays.description: Kick off your shoes and get your hands dirty. Build a lopsided sand castle, dig a tunnel to nowhere, or bury a friend's feet. Grown-ups are fully invited to act like kids.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into the height of summer beach season.
holidays.funFact: Sand castles hold together because of water. Dry sand crumbles, but damp sand clumps as tiny water bridges link the grains.

holidays.name: National Raspberry Bombe Day
holidays.description: A salute to the show-stopping frozen dessert: a round dome of ice cream or sorbet, often layered and filled with raspberry goodness, then sliced to reveal a pretty cross-section.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the classic bombe, a dessert that has been a fancy dinner party centerpiece for generations.
holidays.funFact: "Bombe" is French for bomb. The dessert is named for the round, cannonball-like shape it takes when frozen in a spherical mold.
